title: HostMemory fallback allocation is not checked; commit-limit failure leaves a null backing base
trigger: On Windows, Impl::Init() fails (CreateFileMapping2 SEC_COMMIT of the full intended memory size exceeds the commit limit, or placeholder APIs / 39-bit virtual reserve fail). The ctor falls back to VirtualAlloc(MEM_RESERVE|MEM_COMMIT) of backing_size. If the commit limit was the reason for the failure, this fails too, Allocate returns nullptr and backing_base is stored as null.
impact: No clean error: DeviceMemory::GetPointer/GetRawPhysicalAddr/ClearBackingRegion/JIT fastmem math then use a null-based pointer and crash far from the cause. If Init failed for a non-commit reason (missing APIs, virtual reserve failure) the fallback usually succeeds and nothing is seen.

evidence.quote: auto* ptr = VirtualAlloc(nullptr, size, MEM_RESERVE | MEM_COMMIT, PAGE_READWRITE);

reasoning: Allocate logs the failure but returns nullptr and the constructor assigns it without a check; nothing downstream (DeviceMemory ctor, HostMemory::BackingBasePointer users) validates it. Only HintCold checks backing_base for null; ClearBackingRegion and DeviceMemory pointer helpers do not. The fallback commits the same amount as the SEC_COMMIT section, so it fails under the same commit-limit condition. Requires a commit-starved host, hence narrow.
fix_note: Check the result and fail loudly (LOG_CRITICAL plus throw/abort with the requested size) - correct and harmless. A smaller/lazy (SEC_RESERVE) backing is a larger change; the fixed layout size is assumed everywhere.

title: BuildTransform mask is wrong for writes that cross a 2 KiB chunk (shift count underflows)
trigger: Any CPU write to a rasterizer-cached page whose [addr&0x7FF, +size) range passes the 2 KiB chunk end (page_bits = DEVICE_PAGEBITS-1 = 11). E.g. WriteBlock/ZeroBlock/CopyBlock of a full 4 KiB guest page: HandleRasterizerWrite(addr, 4096) -> Collect(0x10000,4096): minor_address=0, top_bit=(0+4096+63)>>6=64, shift count 32-64 wraps in size_t to 2^64-32, UB; x86 shl uses count mod 32 so the shifts are no-ops, mask=0xFFFFFFFF covering only the first 2 KiB chunk; the chunk at 0x10800 is never recorded.
impact: GPU cache invalidation (OnCacheInvalidations via Gather) misses the upper part of the write: stale buffer/texture/shader data for CPU-written memory (flicker, wrong geometry/textures). Actual codegen of the UB shift is compiler-dependent, but the second chunk is never recorded in any case.

evidence.quote: const size_t top_bit = (minor_address + size + align_mask) >> align_bits;

reasoning: WalkBlock splits at guest 4 KiB pages, so copy_amount can be up to 4096 and the lambda gets a device address with the in-page offset, and size is passed whole to Collect. Collect/BuildTransform record only one 2 KiB chunk (single u32 mask, one address) and never split by chunk. Any size > 2048 - (addr&0x7FF) overflows top_bit past 32. Tests only use 4/8/128 bytes within a chunk, so this is untested. Small straddling writes (e.g. 16 bytes at 0x7F8) hit the same underflow.
fix_note: Suggested fix is right: loop in Collect over chunk boundaries calling BuildTransform on each clipped piece (each piece <= 2 KiB, top_bit <= 32; also special-case top_bit==32 where u32 shifts by 0 are fine). Cost: up to two Collects per 4 KiB write, hot path (atomic CAS); keep the same-chunk fast path.
